summary: In the τ²-bench airline domain, tools accept forbidden writes silently, and 78% of a budget agent's failures are wrong final states with no tool error. Four hand-written, read-only Python predicates check each proposed write against database state before it runs. They raise gpt-4o-mini success from 29.6% to 42.0%, and the lift replicates on 15 disjoint seeds. Almost all of it comes from one 100%-precision gate, and negative controls on retail and BFCL show little or no gain where tools already enforce their own preconditions.

claims.claim: A four-gate deterministic pre-execution suite raises gpt-4o-mini success on τ²-bench airline from 29.6% to 42.0%, and the lift replicates
claims.evidence: Table 2: 74/250→105/250 (+12.4 pp, CI [+4.0, +21.2], P=0.0012); disjoint 15-seed replication 231/750→323/750 (+12.3 pp, P=0.0008). Paired task-level bootstrap. Replication is over seeds on the same 50 tasks the gates were written against (§7 item 8).

claims.claim: The lift is carried by where gates fire, and mostly by one high-precision gate
claims.evidence: Table 3: firing stratum +19.2 pp (CI [+6.9, +33.1]) vs non-firing +5.0 pp (CI spans zero). Table 6: cancellation_eligibility 161/161 true blocks and the only gate whose removal lowers pass1; baggage_allowance 5% precision.

claims.claim: Gates help only where tools are policy-permissive; they add little where tools self-enforce
claims.evidence: §6.1: retail 8 tasks, 62.5%→57.8% (CI spans zero, partly an encoding bug). §6.2: BFCL 0 firings in 200 entries. The negative controls are small and the retail one is confounded by a gate bug.

claims.claim: The failure mode persists for a frontier model (gpt-5.2): gates lift 61.2%→71.6%
claims.evidence: §5.3: n=5 per task, unreplicated, CI [+0.4, +20.8]; three tasks regress with gate firings. Authors label it suggestive.

claims.claim: Gates beat model reasoning on deceptive inputs
claims.evidence: §5.6: task #48 (user asserts false context) solved 16/16 gated vs ≤1/16 ungated across settings. A single task; no prompting or reflection baseline was tested (§7 item 7).

patterns.note: Deterministic predicates over (tool, args, DB state) at the write boundary lift task success with replication; precision must be audited per gate; one domain.
Explicitly contrasts gates with LLM judges and reflection, but does not run either as a baseline.
Per-gate fire/precision audit against ground-truth trajectories is a useful observability practice; not the paper's focus.

methodology.sample: 50 τ²-bench airline tasks × 5 trials (plus 15-seed replication, 750 trials); 8 retail tasks; 200 BFCL v4 entries
methodology.baselines: Same harness without gates; no prompt-the-rule or reflection baseline
methodology.models: gpt-4o-mini agent (main), gpt-5.2 (suggestive), gpt-4.1 user simulator
methodology.variance: Paired task-level bootstrap CIs (20k resamples); pass^k; disjoint-seed replication
methodology.ablations: Minus-one gate removal, per-gate precision, firing stratification, curated-subset inflation
methodology.contamination_controls: Not applicable to a gate intervention; gates were written from policy and evaluated on the same tasks (acknowledged)
methodology.languages: Python harness; customer-service domain, no code generation

standards.artifacts: Code and gate predicates 'will be released upon publication'; none found

biases.detail: Gates were authored against the same 50 tasks; replication varies seeds, not tasks.
No baseline that states the gated rules more forcefully in the prompt or adds reflection.
Replicated result is gpt-4o-mini only; the frontier arm is unreplicated.
One simulated airline domain with an LLM user simulator.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: OpenAI models as agents; no own product
coi.detail: No vendor tie; the intervention is not a product.

verdict_reason: Unusually well-bounded: replication, firing stratification, per-gate precision audit and negative controls, and limitations are stated plainly. Caveats: one positive domain, gates fitted to the evaluated tasks, no prompt baseline, artifacts unreleased.
applicability: The transferable lesson is about where policy lives. If a tool accepts writes that policy forbids, put a deterministic state-reading predicate in front of it, or better, make the tool self-enforce. Audit each gate's precision, because a bad gate costs success. For a Java team this maps to agent-facing write tools (content publish, delivery API mutations) and CI gates. It says nothing about the runtime that hosts the predicates (Python vs WASM) or about gates over build artifacts.

conflicts_with.detail: That paper finds classifier and prompt guardrails routinely bypassed; this one finds state-reading deterministic gates hold. They agree once guardrail type is distinguished: probabilistic content filters vs deterministic state predicates.
